The reconstruction is a model estimate from those detections; the frames are the passes NASA's CMR granule list gives over the region, with their geometry.

orbit_node_rule.rule: orbit_node is the platform's equator-crossing node on the day side of its sun-synchronous orbit for a day pass (is_day true) and the opposite node for a night pass
orbit_node_rule.note: Terra and Aqua have drifted from their design crossing times; the node direction is unchanged.

observer_passes.geometry_note: FIRMS does not publish a pass's geometry. scan_angle_deg, view_zenith_deg, azimuth_deg, subsat_lon and subsat_lat are worked out from where the region box lies in the swath polygon of the pass, which NASA's CMR granule list gives; no detection is read for them, so a held-out frame has them too. cloud_fraction is not measured (FIRMS rows carry no cloud mask) and is written as 0; granule_cloud_cover_pct is the mean over a whole MODIS granule, about 2,000 km long, and is null for VIIRS.
observer_passes.confidence_note: MODIS confidence is the source's 0 to 100 value. VIIRS confidence is a class; the numeric slot holds 15, 55 or 90 for low, nominal, high and the class counts are in each frame's viirs_confidence_classes.

parameters.fitted_on: 22 real fire episodes of 2018, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2021 in the plumas_ca, lytton_bc and evia_greece context boxes, the three 2021 test fires excluded (backend/model/episodes.py)

learned_parts.name: reconstruction parameters
learned_parts.detail: fitted values are used: on validation fires they are ahead of both baselines on 2 of 7 scores, tied on 5 and behind on none, beyond the noise of resampling the fires
learned_parts.rule: validation fires are resampled whole (2,000 times); a score is ahead when the 90 percent interval of its improvement over each baseline is above zero, behind when it is below zero against one of them, a tie otherwise. The fitted values are used when no score is behind and at least one is ahead. A part is on when every score of the part is ahead (and, for FRP, the 90 percent interval held for at least 80 percent of validation overpasses); otherwise the part is experimental.
learned_parts.trained_on: 22 real fire episodes of 2018, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2021 in the plumas_ca, lytton_bc and evia_greece context boxes, the three 2021 test fires excluded (backend/model/episodes.py)
learned_parts.validated_on: 7 real fire episodes of 2024, 2025 in the same three context boxes (other years than training; none of them a test fire)

encoding.byte_zero: no fire: the value is exactly zero
encoding.encode: byte = 0 when v is 0; otherwise 1 + round(254 * log10(v / min) / log10(max / min)), kept within 1 to 255
encoding.decode: v = 0 when byte is 0; otherwise min * (max / min) ** ((byte - 1) / 254)

channels.a: VIIRS FRP density as observed (only on VIIRS frames)

encoding.applies_to: all four channels of reconstruction_u8.bin and the density byte of belief_u8.bin, real runs only
encoding.simulated_runs: unchanged: linear, 0 to 80 MW/km2 for r, b and a, 0 to 24 for g
encoding.why: real FRP densities on 375 m cells span about six decades (0.003 to 7,132 MW/km2 in the nine windows measured); on the linear 0 to 80 scale 28 percent of observed cells and 4 percent of reconstructed cells were clipped
encoding.grid: 375 m cells shown on the 256 by 256 tensor grid by nearest cell
encoding.note: counts are 375 m cells over the 24 frames; a cell above the scale is written as the maximum and one below the floor as the floor; epoch_summaries and each frame's mean and max carry the exact values

belief_frames.layout: steps x ny x nx x 2, uint8, C order

channels.name: expected_frp_density
channels.decode: v = 0 when byte is 0; otherwise min * (max / min) ** ((byte - 1) / 254)

belief_frames.view: forward filter only: each step uses the overpasses assimilated up to its time, so the belief spreads between passes and tightens at each one. The 24 payload frames hold the smoothed estimate instead.

fit_residuals.source: NASA FIRMS standard processing archive (MODIS Collection 6.1, VIIRS 375 m Collection 2), read through backend.firms

protocol.name: sealed hidden rows, schedule from the pass list, empty passes scored
protocol.rule: with an instrument hidden, the window, the estimate, the declared cells, the intervals, the belief frames, the exports and an agent's observation are built from the visible rows only; the hidden rows are opened by the scorer alone, after every prediction is fixed
protocol.replaces: version 2, in which predictions were published at nominal half-day slots with a typical pixel size and only hidden overpasses that left a detection were scored

fit_residuals.hidden_platforms_from: the archive's start dates (backend/model/platforms.py), not the hidden rows
fit_residuals.visible_rows_note: visible_rows_in_test_box counts every visible row the methods were given whose pixel centre lies in the test box, whatever its time. A caller hands the methods more than the scored window (a run keeps two days either side, because the estimate is a reconstruction and not a forecast), so the count is larger than the rows of the window alone, which is visible_rows_in_test_box_inside_window.

definitions.truth: At each scored overpass of the hidden instrument: the 375 m cells whose centre lies inside one of its flagged pixels (real scan by track footprint), and the sum of its FRP over pixels centred in the box. This is what the hidden instrument reported, not the fire itself.
definitions.predicted_cells: The 375 m cells a method declares. A method that gives only a probability field is cut at 0.5 (the baselines paint 0 or 1). The reconstruction declares its N most probable cells, N being the number of cells it expects to be flagged (the sum of its probabilities): a coarse pixel says fire is somewhere inside it, so an honest probability is rarely above 0.5 and a fixed cut would declare nothing.
definitions.equal_area: Every method cut to the same number of cells: its N most probable cells, N being the number of cells the painted MODIS baseline declares at that overpass (ties go to larger expected FRP, then grid order). Hit rate and false alarm ratio at equal area compare where a method puts fire, not how much it declares.
definitions.hit_rate: TP / (TP + FN): the share of truth cells that are predicted cells. Undefined when there is no truth cell.
definitions.false_alarm_ratio: FP / (TP + FP): the share of predicted cells that are not truth cells. Undefined with no predicted cell.
definitions.false_alarm_rate: FP / (FP + TN): the share of cells without a hidden detection that are predicted cells.
definitions.csi: TP / (TP + FP + FN): critical success index, one number that falls with both misses and false alarms.
definitions.tolerant_scores: The same four scores with a one cell (375 m) tolerance: a truth cell is hit when a predicted cell lies within one cell of it, and a predicted cell is a false alarm only when no truth cell lies within one cell.
definitions.brier: Mean over all cells of (probability minus truth as 0 or 1) squared. Lower is better.
definitions.cell_rmse: Root mean square difference between predicted and hidden FRP density (MW per km2 of a 375 m cell), over the cells where either is above zero, pooled over the scored overpasses.
definitions.frp_total_error: Per overpass, predicted total FRP in the box minus the hidden instrument's total, divided by the hidden total (signed, so minus 0.5 means half). Summarised by its median, by the median absolute value, and by the ratio of the two totals summed over the scored overpasses. Overpasses with a hidden total of zero are left out of the relative figures and counted.
definitions.pixel_count: The number of pixels the hidden instrument flags in the box at an overpass, against the number a method expects. Summarised like FRP: ratio of the sums over the scored overpasses, median signed and median absolute relative error, and the coverage of a stated interval. This is the currency of the calendar (hotspot counts), so it is where the overlap ratio baseline makes its own prediction.
definitions.interval_coverage: The share of scored overpasses whose hidden total FRP lies inside the method's stated interval, next to the level the method states (for example 0.90). A method that states no interval is reported as stating none.
definitions.pooling: Cell counts TP, FP, FN, TN are summed over the scored overpasses of a run before the ratios are taken, so large overpasses weigh more. Scored overpasses are those of the hidden instrument seen anywhere in the wider context box; one with no detection inside the test box contributes only false alarms and true negatives.

schedule.note: one slot per pass of a hidden platform whose swath holds the whole box, from NASA CMR granule metadata: the time the scan crossed the box and the pixel size there, both from the swath polygon. Nothing is read from the hidden rows. A pass with no hidden detection is scored as a look that flagged nothing; VIIRS granules carry no cloud information and MODIS cloud cover is a granule mean, so such a look may have been cloudy.

painted_modis.label: MODIS detections painted onto the cells they cover (nearest overpass in time, within 12 h)

overlap_ratio.label: painted MODIS cells; pixel count = calendar overlap ratio 2.532 times (nearest Terra + nearest Aqua pixels); FRP times one overlap ratio 0.814 (from 2685 pairs: real FIRMS rows of plumas_ca, lytton_bc, evia_greece context boxes, years 2018, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2021, with the three 2021 test fires excluded (backend/model/training.py)); FRP interval from the 5th to 95th percentile of pair ratios

overlap_ratio_fit.definition: Pairs are one MODIS overpass and the VIIRS overpass nearest in time, at most 90 minutes apart, both with detections in the training rows given. ratio = sum of VIIRS FRP / sum of MODIS FRP over all pairs; the percentiles are of the per pair ratios.

calendar_overlap_ratio.definition: Suomi NPP rows over Terra plus Aqua rows across the overlap months of the region's context box (the monthly counts of backend/firms/real_calendar.py, months with an outage day left out as the calendar does), fitted without the run's year and without any year that holds a test fire; p10 and p90 are percentiles of the kept years' ratios
